ai.budget_hint: The run stops when the next request would exceed the limit. Empty = no limit.

ai.estimate_cost: Estimated cost: {{cost}}. Already spent on the project: {{spent}}.
ai.started: Run started. Progress shows at the top of the page.
ai.calibration_hint: Compares the AI answers with the human decisions. “Maybe” counts as include, since it does not drop the study.
ai.sensitivity_hint: Of the studies humans included, how many the AI also included.
ai.specificity_hint: Of the studies humans excluded, how many the AI also excluded.
ai.confusion: Included by both: {{tp}} · AI excluded an included one: {{fn}} · Excluded by both: {{tn}} · AI included an excluded one: {{fp}} · “Maybe” answers: {{maybe}}
ai.low_recall: Sensitivity is below 95%. Review the criteria or use the AI only as a suggestion.
ai.no_calibration: No AI answers for human-decided records yet. Run a calibration.

ai.usage: AI usage on this project: {{calls}} calls, {{tokens}} tokens, {{cost}}.

ai.stop_after: Suggest stopping after N excludes in a row

ai.curve_hint: The curve shows how many included records appeared along the screening. When it flattens, most relevant records have been found.
ai.embed_hint: Needed before prioritizing. Only computes what is new.
ai.curve_stats: {{screened}} of {{total}} screened, {{found}} included. Excludes in a row since the last include: {{since}}.
ai.curve_expected: Estimated relevant records among the unscreened: {{n}}.
ai.prioritized_on: The queue is ordered by the model.
ai.prioritized_off: The queue is not prioritized yet (turn the option on, compute embeddings and decide at least one include and one exclude).

ai.task_extraction_hint: Model that reads the PDFs and fills the fields marked in the extraction forms. Needs a long context (32k tokens or more).
ai.task_chat_hint: Model that answers questions about the PDFs. If left empty, the screening model is used.

sources.title: Search a database directly
sources.hint: ReValli queries the database through its public API and imports the results as a search, with date and strategy recorded for PRISMA-S.
sources.syntax_pubmed: Same syntax as the PubMed site: MeSH terms with [mh], fields such as [tiab], AND, OR, NOT and truncation with *. Tags from other databases (ti:, ab:) are replaced by [ti] and [tiab].
sources.syntax_openalex: Searches title and abstract: words, quoted phrases, uppercase AND, OR and NOT and parentheses. Fields such as ti: and ab: do not exist here and are corrected to title and abstract. Truncation with *: switches to exact search, with no word stemming.
sources.syntax_europepmc: Fields such as TITLE:, ABSTRACT:, TITLE_ABS: and KW:, with AND, OR and NOT. Tags from other databases (ti:, [tiab]) are replaced by the ones used here.
sources.started: Import started. Progress shows at the top of the page and the references join screening when it finishes.
sources.over_limit: Only the first {{limit}} will be imported. Refine the strategy or raise the limit.
sources.ignored: The database ignored these terms and ran the rest of the strategy:
sources.translation: How the database interpreted the strategy
sources.last_search: Last search: {{imported}} of {{found}} results imported from {{source}}.
sources.last_truncated: Some results were left out by the limit.
sources.translate_title: Translate the strategy to another database (AI)
sources.translate_hint: The AI adapts fields, controlled vocabulary and operators to the chosen database syntax. It uses the configured screening model and counts toward the project budget.
sources.translate_review: AI translation ({{model}}). Review the terms and check the number of results before using it.
sources.snowball_hint: Uses OpenAlex to find what the included studies cite and what cites them. References already in the project are skipped; new ones join screening as a citation search, reported separately in PRISMA.
sources.seeds_one: {{count}} study included at full text will be used as a seed.
sources.seeds_other: {{count}} studies included at full text will be used as seeds.
sources.no_seeds: There are no studies included at full text to use as seeds yet.
sources.dir_both_hint: References of the included studies and works citing them.
sources.dir_backward_hint: Only the reference lists of the included studies.
sources.dir_forward_hint: Only later works that cite the included studies.
sources.result_known_one: {{count}} hit was already in the project.
sources.result_known_other: {{count}} hits were already in the project.
sources.syntax_scielo: OpenAlex search on title and abstract, restricted to the journals of the SciELO Brazil collection: words, quoted phrases, uppercase AND, OR and NOT and parentheses. Fields such as ti: and ab: are corrected to title and abstract. Use Portuguese and Spanish terms. Truncation with *: switches to exact search.
sources.syntax_pepsic: OpenAlex search on title and abstract, restricted to PePSIC journals: same syntax as OpenAlex (words, quotes, AND, OR, NOT, parentheses). Fields such as ti: and ab: are corrected. Truncation with *: switches to exact search.
sources.no_direct: LILACS/BVS and the CAPES Portal have no direct search (anti-bot block, key required, or no API). Use strategy translation, export from the portal and import the file. SciELO and PePSIC here are OpenAlex's coverage of those journals, not the SciELO search engine.
sources.assist_title: Chat with the AI to build the search
sources.assist_intro: Explain what you want to research and in which databases. The AI says what it understood, asks questions if something is missing and writes the strategy for each database for you to copy.
sources.assist_placeholder: E.g. I want to search for the iatrogenic effects of talking about bullying, in PubMed and SciELO
sources.assist_reply_placeholder: Answer the questions or ask for changes (more synonyms, another database, narrowing…)
sources.assist_hint: Ctrl+Enter sends. Always check the count in the database before importing.
sources.assist_wait: The first answer can take longer while the model loads into memory.
sources.assist_saved: The conversation is saved for you in this project. Only the latest exchanges are kept.
sources.builder_hint: One row per concept. Within a row, use OR between synonyms and quotes for phrases. Only the fields this database supports are offered.
sources.or_hint: In this database, OR only works inside the same field (title and abstract are merged). Other cases become AND, and we tell you.
sources.placeholder_default: Terms: synonyms with OR, phrases in quotes
sources.fixed_title: We corrected the strategy for this database:
sources.fix_field_tags_removed: The fields {{detail}} do not exist in this database; the search ran on title and abstract.
sources.fix_field_tags_converted: The fields {{detail}} were replaced by this database's own fields.
sources.fix_field_unavailable: This database has no {{detail}} field; we used title and abstract.
sources.fix_pubmed_tags_removed: PubMed field tags in square brackets that this database does not recognise were removed.
sources.fix_operators_uppercased: The operators and, or and not were put in uppercase.
sources.fix_or_merged_title_abstract: OR between title and abstract was merged into a single title-and-abstract field.
sources.fix_or_across_fields: This database does not accept OR between different fields ({{detail}}); we used AND.
sources.fix_year_invalid: The year “{{detail}}” was not understood and the row was ignored. Use 2020 or 2015-2020.

prisma2020.1: Identify the report as a systematic review.
prisma2020.2: Structured abstract (see the PRISMA 2020 for Abstracts checklist).
prisma2020.3: Rationale: describe the review in the context of existing knowledge.
prisma2020.4: Objectives: state explicitly the objectives or questions the review addresses.
prisma2020.5: Eligibility criteria: inclusion and exclusion criteria, and how studies were grouped for the syntheses.
prisma2020.6: Information sources: databases, registers, websites, organisations and reference lists searched, with the date each was last searched.
prisma2020.7: Search strategy: full strategies for all databases, registers and websites, including filters and limits.
prisma2020.8: Selection process: how many reviewers screened each record, whether independently, and any automation tools used.
prisma2020.9: Data collection: how many reviewers collected data from each report, whether independently, contact with authors and automation tools.
prisma2020.10a: Outcomes: list and define the outcomes sought and which results from each study were collected.
prisma2020.10b: Other variables: list and define other variables (participants, intervention, funding) and assumptions about missing information.
prisma2020.11: Risk of bias: tool used, how many reviewers assessed each study, whether independently, and automation tools.
prisma2020.12: Effect measures: the measure used for each outcome (e.g. risk ratio, mean difference).
prisma2020.13a: Synthesis: how studies were chosen for each synthesis.
prisma2020.13b: Synthesis: how data were prepared for presentation or synthesis (missing data, conversions).
prisma2020.13c: Synthesis: methods to tabulate or visually display results.
prisma2020.13d: Synthesis: methods used and rationale; for meta-analysis, model, heterogeneity and software.
prisma2020.13e: Synthesis: methods to explore causes of heterogeneity (subgroups, meta-regression).
prisma2020.14: Reporting bias: methods to assess risk of bias due to missing results.
prisma2020.15: Certainty assessment: methods to assess certainty in the body of evidence (e.g. GRADE).
prisma2020.16a: Study selection: results of the search and selection, ideally with a flow diagram.
prisma2020.16b: Study selection: studies that seemed eligible but were excluded, and why.
prisma2020.17: Study characteristics: cite each included study and present its characteristics.
prisma2020.18: Risk of bias in studies: assessment for each included study.
prisma2020.19: Results of individual studies: summary statistics per group and effect estimate with precision, for each outcome.
prisma2020.20a: Syntheses: summary of characteristics and risk of bias of contributing studies.
prisma2020.20b: Syntheses: results of each synthesis; for meta-analysis, estimate, interval and heterogeneity.
prisma2020.20c: Syntheses: results of investigations of heterogeneity.
prisma2020.21: Reporting biases: risk of bias due to missing results for each synthesis.
prisma2020.22: Certainty of evidence: certainty for each outcome assessed.
prisma2020.23a: Discussion: general interpretation of results in the context of other evidence.
prisma2020.23b: Discussion: limitations of the evidence included.
prisma2020.23c: Discussion: limitations of the review processes.
prisma2020.23d: Discussion: implications for practice, policy and future research.
prisma2020.24a: Registration: register name and number, or a statement that it was not registered.
prisma2020.24b: Protocol: where it can be accessed, or a statement that none was prepared.
prisma2020.24c: Amendments to the registration or protocol.
prisma2020.25: Support: sources of funding and role of funders.
prisma2020.27: Availability of data, code and other materials (forms, extracted data, analyses).

prisma_scr.1: Identify the report as a scoping review.
prisma_scr.2: Structured summary: background, objectives, criteria, sources, charting methods, results and conclusions.
prisma_scr.3: Rationale: what is already known and why a scoping review.
prisma_scr.4: Objectives: questions and objectives with their key elements (population, concept, context).
prisma_scr.5: Protocol and registration: whether one exists, where to access it and registration number.
prisma_scr.6: Eligibility criteria for sources of evidence, with rationale.
prisma_scr.7: Information sources: databases, coverage dates, contact with authors and date of the last search.
prisma_scr.8: Search: full strategy for at least one database, with limits, so it can be repeated.
prisma_scr.9: Selection of sources of evidence: screening and eligibility process.
prisma_scr.10: Data charting: methods (tested forms, independence, duplication, confirmation with authors).
prisma_scr.11: Data items: list and define the variables sought and assumptions made.
prisma_scr.12: Critical appraisal (if done): methods and how the information was used in the synthesis.
prisma_scr.13: Synthesis of results: methods for handling and summarising the charted data.
prisma_scr.14: Selection of sources: numbers screened, assessed and included, with reasons for exclusion, ideally in a flow diagram.
prisma_scr.15: Characteristics of sources: for each source, the characteristics of the charted data.
prisma_scr.17: Results of individual sources: relevant data related to the objectives.
prisma_scr.18: Synthesis: summarise or present the charting results as they relate to the questions.
prisma_scr.19: Summary of evidence: main results, concepts, themes and types of evidence, linked to the objectives.
prisma_scr.20: Limitations of the scoping review process.
prisma_scr.21: Conclusions: general interpretation, implications and next steps.
prisma_scr.22: Funding: sources and role of funders.

checklist.title: Reporting checklist
checklist.hint: Record where each item is addressed in the manuscript. When it can, ReValli shows project data that helps write the item.
checklist.fact_strategies: {{with}} of {{total}} searches have the strategy recorded (Import tab).
checklist.fact_screening: Title and abstract: {{ta}} reviewer(s) per record; full text: {{ft}}. {{blind}}
checklist.fact_ai: AI used in screening ({{mode}}){{local}}; report the model and how it was used.
checklist.fact_no_rob: No risk of bias form created.
checklist.fact_prisma: {{identified}} records identified, {{duplicates}} duplicates, {{screened}} screened, {{included}} studies included. The flow diagram is above.
checklist.fact_coding: {{codes}} codes and {{excerpts}} excerpts in the qualitative coding.
checklist.fact_exports: Forms and extracted data can be downloaded as CSV in the Extraction tab.

coding.title: Qualitative coding
coding.hint: Create codes (themes and subthemes), mark excerpts of the included studies and see the code-by-study matrix.
coding.name: Name
coding.delete_confirm: Delete the code “{{name}}” and its subcodes? Excerpts left without a code are deleted too.
coding.merge_confirm: Merge “{{from}}” into “{{into}}”? Its excerpts and subcodes move to “{{into}}”.
coding.no_codes: No codes yet. Create the first one to start coding.
coding.matrix_hint: Each cell shows how many excerpts of the study carry the code (including subcodes). Click to see them.
coding.no_studies: No studies included at full text yet.
coding.selection_hint: Select an excerpt in the PDF with the mouse and click the codes to mark it.
coding.no_excerpts: No excerpts marked in this study.

meta.title: Meta-analysis
meta.hint: Pool the results of included studies into a single estimate, with forest plot, heterogeneity and funnel plot. Calculations run on the server (inverse variance; DerSimonian-Laird random effects).
meta.name: Analysis name
meta.lower_favours_1: Lower values favour group 1 (e.g. undesirable outcome)
meta.columns_hint_RR: Enter events and total participants for each group.
meta.columns_hint_OR: Enter events and total participants for each group. Zero cells get a 0.5 correction.
meta.columns_hint_RD: Enter events and total participants for each group.
meta.columns_hint_MD: Enter n, mean and standard deviation for each group.
meta.columns_hint_SMD: Enter n, mean and standard deviation for each group. The effect is Hedges' g.
meta.columns_hint_HR: Enter the hazard ratio and 95% confidence interval reported by the study.
meta.columns_hint_GENERIC: Enter the effect (already on the log scale for ratios) and its standard error.
meta.paste_hint: One row per study, tab-separated columns: {{cols}}
meta.delete_confirm: Delete this meta-analysis? GRADE rows linked to it lose the link.
meta.subgroup_test: Test for subgroup differences: Q = {{q}} (df = {{df}}, p {{p}})
meta.no_data: No studies with enough data to calculate yet.
meta.corrected_note: Studies with zero events in one group received a 0.5 continuity correction.
meta.egger_few: With fewer than 10 studies the test has low power; interpret with caution.

grade.title: GRADE: certainty of evidence
grade.hint: Rate the certainty of evidence for each outcome and build the summary of findings table. Certainty starts high for randomised trials and low for observational studies and changes with the domains.
grade.design_hint: Sets the starting level of certainty.
grade.effect_hint: Relative effect and, optionally, absolute effect (e.g. 30 fewer per 1,000).
grade.tip_imprecision_crosses_null: The 95% CI crosses the line of no effect.
grade.tip_publication_bias_few_studies: Fewer than 10 studies: the funnel plot and Egger's test say little.
grade.tip_publication_bias_egger: Egger's test p < 0.10 suggests funnel asymmetry.
grade.tips_after_save: Save to see suggestions calculated from the meta-analysis.
grade.delete_confirm: Delete this outcome from the table?

report_doc.title: Review report (DOCX or PDF)
report_doc.hint: Generates a draft with methods, results (PRISMA flow diagram, included studies, risk of bias, meta-analyses, GRADE and codes) and appendices with the searches, the log of AI use and the checklist. The text is built from the project's data: review it before use.

corpus.title: Chat with the PDFs
corpus.hint: Ask about the studies and get an answer built only from what the PDFs say, with the passage and page behind each claim. Every citation is looked up in the PDF text.
corpus.not_enabled: AI is turned off in this project. Turn it on in the AI tab.
corpus.no_model: No chat model configured. The administrator picks one in the AI settings.
corpus.text_only: Keyword search only (no embeddings model configured)
corpus.empty: No PDF with text has been indexed yet. Upload the PDFs in the References tab and index them.
corpus.question: Question
corpus.placeholder: E.g.: What were the dose and duration of the intervention in the studies?
corpus.no_hits: No PDF passage matches the question. Try other words or search all PDFs.
corpus.not_grounded: No citation could be checked against the PDF text. Treat this answer as unreliable.
corpus.unverified: quote not found in the PDF
corpus.numbers: Numbers in the answer that do not appear in the cited passages: {{list}}. Check the PDF before using them.
corpus.embeddings_unsupported: The embeddings model “{{model}}” cannot produce embeddings (it looks like a chat model). The passages were indexed and search falls back to keywords. Pick an embeddings model such as bge-m3 on the AI page and index again.
corpus.embeddings_failed: Embeddings were not computed ({{error}}). The passages were indexed and search falls back to keywords.

account.tokens_hint: A key gives read-only access to your projects through the API, with the same blinding you have in the interface. Use it for scripts and for the MCP server. Keep it like a password.
account.token_once: Copy it now: the key will not be shown again.
account.password_saved: Password changed. Other sessions of this account were signed out.

watches.title: Automatic updates
watches.hint: Repeats a search, or rereads a file at a URL (RIS, BibTeX, CSL JSON...), at the chosen interval and imports only what the project does not have yet. Each round with news is recorded as an “(update)” search for PRISMA-S. New records go to screening.
watches.name: Name (optional)
watches.url_hint: Addresses inside the server's network are refused.
watches.secret_hint: E.g.: Bearer abc123. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.
watches.last_result: Last round: {{new}} new of {{found}} found (total so far: {{total}}).
watches.news: {{count}} new records from “{{name}}” are waiting for screening.
watches.error_blocked_address: the address points to the internal network
watches.error_unknown_format: the file is not a known references format
watches.error_dns_failed: the server name was not found

gaps.title: Evidence gap map
gaps.hint: Crosses two dimensions of the included studies, for example intervention × outcome. Each cell counts the studies in both categories; empty (dashed) cells are the gaps. Dimensions come from qualitative codes (the subcodes of a code) or from the choice fields of extraction forms.
gaps.no_dimensions: No dimensions yet: create codes with subcodes in the Synthesis tab, or choice fields in an extraction form.
gaps.legend: Numbers are studies. “Unclassified” gathers studies with no category in that dimension. A study can appear in several categories.

project_settings.delete_hint: Permanently deletes the project, its {{count}} records, PDFs, decisions, extractions and everything else. This cannot be undone.
project_settings.type_title: To confirm, type the project name: {{title}}

ai_panel.new_tag: New tag, not in the project vocabulary
ai_panel.show_first: Show the AI suggestion before I decide
ai_panel.hidden: The AI suggestion appears after you decide.
ai_panel.none: The AI has not analysed this record yet.
ai_panel.reason_needs_lead: This reason is not in the protocol yet. Ask a lead to create it.
ai_panel.new_reason: New exclusion reason (edit if you like)

ai_screen.title: AI screening
ai_screen.intro: The AI reads the records that have no decision yet and suggests include, exclude or maybe, with the reason and up to 4 tags. You decide in the screening session.
ai_screen.enable: Turn on AI for this project
ai_screen.nothing: There are no pending records for the AI to analyse.
ai_screen.stopped: Screening stopped: {{done}} of {{total}} records analysed. What was done is saved.
ai_screen.redo_hint: Continue only analyses the missing records. Redo analyses all of them again and replaces the saved answers (it has a cost with a remote model).
ai_screen.stopped_quota: Screening stopped: the AI provider's daily quota ran out ({{done}} of {{total}} analysed). What was done is saved; use Continue tomorrow or switch providers.
ai_screen.stopped_budget: Screening stopped by the project's spending cap ({{done}} of {{total}} analysed). What was done is saved.

protocol_ai.not_configured: AI is not configured on this installation yet (provider and screening model).
protocol_ai.not_enabled: AI is turned off for this project. Turn it on in the AI tab.
protocol_ai.criteria_intro: The AI reads the criteria you wrote above, splits them into items, defines how to apply each one and flags doubts. You review, edit and save; only then does screening use this list instead of the text.
protocol_ai.write_first: Write and save the criteria above first.
protocol_ai.uses_saved: Uses the saved criteria text above.
protocol_ai.questions: The AI has questions about the criteria:
protocol_ai.answers_placeholder: Answer here in free text and ask it to reorganise.
protocol_ai.no_items: No detailed criteria yet. Screening uses the free text.
protocol_ai.name: Criterion name
protocol_ai.definition: How to decide from the title and abstract
protocol_ai.examples: Examples and borderline cases (one per line)
protocol_ai.in_use: In use for screening: {{count}} detailed criteria.
protocol_ai.back_to_text: Go back to the free text only
protocol_ai.tags_intro: The vocabulary the AI uses to tag each record (up to 4 per record; it may propose 1 new one). Write your own and ask for help completing the list.
protocol_ai.no_tags: No tags yet. Without a vocabulary the AI invents short tags.
protocol_ai.tag_description_placeholder: When to use it (helps the AI)
protocol_ai.suggesting: Reading a sample of the records…
protocol_ai.suggest_hint: The AI reads a sample of your records and completes the vocabulary without repeating yours.
protocol_ai.proposals: AI proposals (tick the ones you want)
protocol_ai.reasons_intro: After the AI screens, it leaves a short reason for each exclusion. Here it merges similar ones into a few reasons, reusing the ones you already have. You review, rename and apply.
protocol_ai.reasons_none: There are no suggested reasons yet: run AI screening first.
protocol_ai.go_protocol: Define the criteria in the Protocol
protocol_ai.draft_hint: With no text, the AI proposes a draft from the project title and description.
protocol_ai.to_text_hint: Writes these items into the inclusion and exclusion fields above, one per line, and saves.
protocol_ai.to_text_confirm: This replaces the current inclusion and exclusion text. Continue?

home.subtitle: Pick up where you left off or start a new review.
home.empty_hint: Create the first one: set the topic, bring in the references and invite the team, in three steps.

wizard.title: New review
wizard.title_placeholder: A name that is easy to spot in the list
wizard.description_hint: Research question, topic or any note for the team. You can edit it later.
wizard.references_intro: How will you bring the references in?
wizard.references_import: Import a file or search the databases
wizard.references_import_hint: Opens the Import page as soon as the review is created: RIS, CSV and other formats, or search PubMed, OpenAlex and Europe PMC with AI help.
wizard.references_later_hint: The review opens on the Overview, with the first steps to follow.
wizard.team_alone_hint: One decision per record is enough (we adjust the protocol for you). You can invite people later.
wizard.team_invite_hint: Creates an invite link for each person; send it by email or message.
wizard.invite_links: Invite links (copy and send to each person):
wizard.ai_intro: Do you want AI to help with screening? It reads title and abstract and suggests include, exclude or maybe; you make the decision.
wizard.ai_unavailable: AI is not configured on this installation yet (provider and model). Ask an administrator to set it up under AI in the menu; then you can turn it on in the review.
wizard.ai_on: Turn AI on in this review
wizard.ai_on_hint: Title and abstract of the records will be sent to the configured model. You can cap spending and use local models only later.
wizard.ai_off_hint: Nothing is sent to any model. You screen everything manually.
wizard.ai_where: To turn it on or off later: open the review and use the “AI” button in the header, or the ☰ menu → Setup and team → AI.
wizard.done_ai_on: AI is on. To turn it off: “AI” button in the review header.
wizard.done_ai_off: AI is off. To turn it on: “AI” button in the review header.

reset.title: Set a new password
